candidates.title: Manual's PMA istart layout (bit positions of R/W/X/IR/IW/DID, an E bit, a 4-bit DID at bits 11-8) does not match the encoding the emulator writes into the guest-readable PMA array
candidates.component: Interpreter / machine address ranges (state layout of the PMA array, read by the guest and by the uarch) vs the manual doc/README.md 'PMAs'
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program, ...'); the other side of the contradiction is the manual
candidates.location: doc/README.md 'PMAs' (~lines 7894-7946: table 'Bits 63-12 start | 11-8 DID | 7 IW | 6 IR | 5 X | 4 W | 3 R | 2 E | 1 IO | 0 M' and 'The M, IO, and E bits are mutually exclusive'); src/pmas-constants.hpp PMA_ISTART_shifts (M=0, IO=1, R=2, W=3, X=4, IR=5, IW=6, DID=7 with a 5-bit mask 31<<7, no E bit); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp make_pmas_address_range (PMA array flags R=true, registered with pmas=true, so readable by the main processor); src/address-range.hpp get_istart/pmas_pack_istart.
candidates.description: The manual specifies the first PMA word as start(63-12), DID(11-8), IW(7), IR(6), X(5), W(4), R(3), E(2), IO(1), M(0), says M/IO/E are mutually exclusive, and says the words are 'readable both internally and externally' and that this array 'is how the RISC-V interpreter discovers the available ranges at runtime'. The code packs M(0), IO(1), R(2), W(3), X(4), IR(5), IW(6), DID(7..11, 5 bits) and has no E bit. Every PMA entry therefore decodes differently under the manual. Measured on a default machine (1 MiB RAM, one read-only flash drive): RAM istart low bits 0x0fd decode per manual as M=1 and E=1 (excluded) with DID=0 (empty); the read-only flash drive (0x1a5) decodes as not readable, executable, write-idempotent, DID=1; the CMIO TX buffer (0x46d) as executable, not writable, DID=4 (CLINT); the RX buffer (0x3e5) as not readable, executable, DID=3 (flash); every entry has the manual's E bit set together with M or IO, which the manual says cannot happen. A guest reading the array (an M-mode ld from 0x10000 returns 0x800000fd on both the native and the uarch path) and decoding it as the manual documents gets wrong memory permissions and wrong device ids. The same section also says the ranges in the board table, including the processor shadow and shadow TLB, are 'visible to the main processor' and 'discoverable at runtime via the PMA array'; in the code the shadow state has no PMA entry and a guest load from 0x300 raises a load access fault (the code is what R8 requires, so that part is a manual error).
candidates.trigger: Any guest code (firmware, kernel or application after an input takes control, section 4) that reads the PMA array at 0x10000 and interprets it per the manual; or any independent implementation of the state layout written from the manual. No untrusted machine API caller needed.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from every valid template: the PMA array is part of every machine's hashed state, readable at any privilege level with translation off (M-mode) or mapped by S-mode page tables; section 2 presumes guest-chosen instruction streams reachable. The behavior is deterministic and identical on the native and uarch paths (shared C++), so it is not a divergence between paths.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies. The trigger is guest code reading documented state, not a deliberate machine API change, an untrusted API caller, a non-template snapshot, O1/O2, or an A1-A8 violation. 'The entries about applications exclude what an application loses, never an emulator defect that its guest triggers (R4, R5, R8).'

2 Role: the encoding is produced by the machine address ranges and consumed by the interpreter and uarch program: AUDIT.md 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program ... | Honest operator'. The manual is the other party of the contradiction.

3 High/Medium cases: section 8 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right, the emulator stores PMA attributes (memory permissions) in a layout other than the documented one, an 'undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths' (Medium) in the area R7 lists as 'Address translation and memory permissions'. R7: 'The emulator implements the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them, departing only where the manual documents a deviation.' R13 makes 'The state layout' part of the protocol. Preferred: Medium.

4 Critical (alternative reading): R7 says that in the listed areas 'any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths'. A correct guest that follows the manual to learn which ranges are writable/executable (e.g. to decide where to place code or to validate the rx/tx buffers) is misled; read literally, step 4 rates a violation of R7 at a reachable state Critical. What decides: whether the Medium case may judge that no correct guest relies on the PMA array for isolation or data integrity (Linux uses the DTB, not the array).
5 Low (alternative reading): if the PMA section is treated as an informal description and the code constants (PMA_ISTART_*) as the specification, it is a documentation error with no rule violated.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Critical under literal R7; Low if the manual's table is read as non-normative)
candidates.threat_to_goal: No direct soundness or completeness failure: all emulator paths agree. It breaks the manual as specification of the state layout (R13) and of memory-permission information exposed to the guest (R7): a guest or third-party implementation built from the manual reads every range's permissions and device id wrongly (RAM 'excluded', rx/tx buffers 'executable', read-only flash 'unreadable').
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSPEC/pma.lua (reads every PMA word through the Lua API and decodes both ways) and pma2.lua (M-mode guest 'lui t0,0x10; ld t1,0(t0)': x6=0x800000fd natively and with run_uarch/reset_uarch). Output, e.g.: '0 istart=0x00000000800000fd ... code: M=1 IO=0 R=1 W=1 X=1 IR=1 IW=1 DID=1 | manual: M=1 IO=0 E=1 R=1 W=1 X=1 IR=1 IW=1 DID=0'; '4 istart=0x00000000600003e5 ... code: R=1 W=0 X=0 DID=7 | manual: E=1 R=0 W=0 X=1 IR=1 IW=1 DID=3'. shadow.lua: guest 'ld x6,0x300(x0)' -> mcause=5 (load access fault), although the manual lists the shadow among ranges visible to the main processor and discoverable through the PMA array.
candidates.test_idea: Build a 1 MiB machine (plus a read-only flash drive), have an M-mode guest load the first PMA word of each entry (or read them with read_word), decode with the manual's table, and assert that for RAM M=1, E=0, R=W=X=1 and DID=PMA_MEMORY_DID, for the RX buffer R=1, W=0, X=0, DID=PMA_CMIO_RX_BUFFER_DID, and that no entry has both M (or IO) and E set. Fails (exit 1) on audit/prt2; passes after either the code or the manual's table is changed so they agree (a fix of the manual only must make the parsed table match PMA_ISTART_* shifts).

candidates.title: A guest write to mcycle (csrw/csrrs/csrrc on CSR 0xB00 in M-mode) raises an illegal-instruction exception, an undocumented deviation from the RISC-V privileged specification
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp write_csr_mcycle (~lines 2405-2414) returns execute_status::failure, which execute_csr_RW/SC/SCI turn into raise_illegal_insn_exception; write_csr dispatch (~line 2561). doc/README.md 'The main processor' (~7304-7385) and the rest of the manual never say that mcycle is read-only or that writing it traps.
candidates.description: The RISC-V privileged specification defines mcycle (0xB00) as an MRW counter that M-mode software may write (minstret, its sibling, is writable here: write_csr_minstret adjusts icycleinstret). The emulator instead makes any write to mcycle from M-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception (mcause 2, mtval = the instruction). The deviation is deliberate (mcycle is the dispute clock and R8 forbids the guest from changing it), but the manual, which R7 makes the only place a deviation may be documented, does not mention it: it lists mcycle as a standard register 'advanced at every CPU cycle' and documents no CSR deviations at all.
candidates.trigger: Any guest code running in M-mode (firmware, or input-controlled code after taking control, section 4) that executes csrw/csrrs/csrrc/csrrwi/... with a nonzero source on mcycle.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template by guest code at M-mode; deterministic and identical on native and uarch paths (verified).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: none applies (guest-triggered behavior of the transition function).
2 Role: interpreter/uarch program, Honest operator per AUDIT.md.

3 High/Medium cases: section 8 Medium 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)'. R7: 'departing only where the manual documents a deviation'; the area is 'Traps and interrupts' (an exception the specification does not raise). The behavior itself is what R8 requires ('It can never change the cycle counter'), so the fix is documentation; no correct guest relies on writing mcycle for isolation. Preferred: Medium.
4 Critical (literal R7 reading): 'any deviation ... in these areas' (traps) at a reachable state.

5 Low (alternative): if R8's statement that the guest can never change the cycle counter is read as documenting the deviation, only the manual is incomplete: Low. Note: triage dropped R1-R7-3 (hpmcounter3-31 trap in M-mode) on similar facts; this case differs in that mcycle is a mandatory MRW counter whose writability the specification requires, while hpm counters may be read-only zero.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Low if R8 is read as documenting it)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None to soundness/completeness; violates R7's requirement that deviations be documented in the manual, in the traps area; guest/tool authors following the manual and the RISC-V spec expect the write to succeed.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSPEC/mcycle.lua: native and uarch both give 'csrw mcycle,x0 -> mcause=0x2 mtval=0xb0001073', while 'csrw minstret,x0' retires (pc advances, mcause 0).
candidates.test_idea: M-mode guest executes csrw mcycle, x5; assert that unless the manual's processor section documents mcycle as read-only/trapping, the instruction does not raise an exception (mcause unchanged, pc advanced). Exits 1 on audit/prt2; 0 after documenting the deviation in the manual (the test greps the processor section) or changing the behavior.

candidates.title: CLINT implements an active msip register (writing 1 at 0x02000000 raises a machine software interrupt), but the manual says the only active CLINT addresses are mtime and mtimecmp
candidates.location: src/clint-address-range.cpp do_read_device/do_write_device (msip0 at offset 0, 32-bit only: sets/clears mip.MSIP and returns success_and_serve_interrupts); doc/README.md '#### CLINT' (~7523-7536): 'The active addresses are 0x0200bff8 (mtime) and 0x02004000 (mtimecmp).' src/dtb.cpp advertises 'riscv,clint0' with interrupts-extended MSIP and MTIP.
candidates.description: The manual describes the CLINT as controlling the timer interrupt only and names mtime and mtimecmp as its only active addresses. The code also implements msip0 at offset 0: a 32-bit store of an odd value sets mip.MSIP (a machine software interrupt), an even value clears it, a 32-bit load reads it back; 64-bit accesses fault. It is a guest-reachable interrupt source the manual does not document. The generated DTB names the device 'riscv,clint0', whose binding includes msip, so only the manual is contradicted (unlike R2-DFGUESTSTATE-1, where manual and DTB agreed). Related undocumented device details: mtime writes and 32-bit mtimecmp accesses raise access faults.
candidates.trigger: Guest code at M-mode (or S/U-mode with a mapping, since the CLINT PMA is R/W) storing to 0x02000000.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template; deterministic and identical natively and in the uarch (verified).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: none applies.
2 Role: devices, Honest operator per AUDIT.md.

3 High/Medium: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right, a store to 0x02000000 would be an access fault and could not raise an interrupt; the emulator instead raises MSIP: an undocumented deterministic deviation consistent across paths in the area R7 lists as 'Traps and interrupts' -> Medium.
4 Critical (literal R7): any deviation in 'Traps and interrupts' at a reachable state.
5 Low: if the DTB's 'riscv,clint0' compatible string is accepted as documentation of the standard CLINT register set, the manual is merely incomplete -> Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium / Low (if the DTB compatible string counts as documentation)
candidates.threat_to_goal: No soundness/completeness effect; a guest following the manual does not expect an interrupt source at 0x02000000 (an M-mode store there to probe or clear memory raises MSIP and, with mie.MSIE and mstatus.MIE set, traps).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSPEC/msip.lua: guest 'lui t0,0x2000; li t1,1; sw t1,0(t0); lw t2,0(t0)' -> mip=0x8 (MSIP), x7=1, no exception, both natively and with run_uarch/reset_uarch.
candidates.test_idea: M-mode guest stores 1 (32-bit) to 0x02000000; assert, unless the manual's CLINT section mentions msip, that the store raises a store access fault and mip.MSIP stays 0. Exits 1 on audit/prt2.

candidates.title: cartesi-machine --print-mcycle-root-hashes prints, for the mcycle that ends a rejecting instruction, the content hash of the rejecting machine (from its implied --initial-hash/--final-hash and its start: line) next to and after the canonical revert root hash
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: '... the cartesi-machine CLI ... | Support'); stands in for a tool that computes claims
candidates.location: src/cartesi-machine.lua: '--print-mcycle-root-hashes=' handler (~2521-2542) sets cmdline.initial_hash and cmdline.final_hash; print_root_hash (~2815) prints '<mcycle>: <get_root_hash()>'; mcycle_root_hashes_runner_run (~4123-4168) prints print_root_hash(m) at start:; final hash printing (~4906-4913).
candidates.description: The option's help says it 'prints root hash every 2^log2_mcycle_period cycles, and where the machine stops' and 'implies --initial-hash and --final-hash'. When the run stops at an rx-rejected manual yield, the library correctly returns the revert root hash for that boundary, and the CLI prints it as '<rej>: <revert hash>', but then prints '<rej>: <content hash of the rejecting machine>' from --final-hash in the same format. When the loaded machine is already at the rejected yield (start: at, or no start), it prints the content hash for <rej> twice and the revert hash once. The canonical hash at the boundary that ends the rejecting instruction is the revert root hash (THREAT_MODEL section 2 'Canonical hash'), so the printed series carries two different hashes for one mcycle, the last one non-canonical. Variant of confirmed R1-R6-1 (same tool, different option and site).
candidates.trigger: A trusted CLI user runs --print-mcycle-root-hashes over a window that ends at a rejection, or on a stored machine saved at the rejected yield; any input sender choosing a payload the guest rejects reaches the state.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from the shared valid bare-metal template by delivering 'R' (rejected), all documented operations.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no (guest rejection plus documented CLI option; no untrusted API caller, no non-guaranteed directory).

2 Role: the CLI is Support per AUDIT.md. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims.' The honest-operator library (collect_mcycle_root_hashes) does not share it.

3 Medium: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium', if the printer counts as a tool computing claim material: in the honest-operator role a non-canonical hash at the rejection boundary violates R4 'After a rejection, every hash the honest operator commits to follows R6, however it is computed' and R6 'Every path that produces a hash for a claim, a node or a proof applies the rejection exception'.
4 n/a (support cap).

5 Low: the extra lines come from --initial-hash/--final-hash, documented as the machine's state hash, and R6 says the rejecting machine's 'own root hash is then the content hash of the rejecting machine'; read as diagnostics ('a defect in a tool's diagnostics'), Low. Deciding fact: whether the lines printed by --print-mcycle-root-hashes (same '<mcycle>: <hash>' format) count as claim material.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium if the printer is a tool that computes claims, as triage held for R1-R6-1)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None directly (no deployment runs the CLI). A user building or checking mcycle-level leaves from the printed series picks up, for the rejection boundary, the last printed value, which is not the canonical hash.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSPEC/cli.lua and cli2.lua with the baremetal-template config: window ending at the rejection prints '3526406: 0x428a6bb8...' (revert root hash, canonical) followed by '3526406: 0x737e2f9a...' (content hash); starting on the stored rejecting machine prints '3526406: 0x737e2f9a...' twice and '3526406: 0x428a6bb8...' once.
candidates.test_idea: Store the template after delivering a rejected input and running to the rejection; run cartesi-machine --load=<dir> --print-mcycle-root-hashes=0 [--max-mcycle=rej+3]; collect all '<rej>: <hash>' lines and assert each equals the revert root hash (or that only one hash is printed per mcycle and it is canonical). Exits 1 on audit/prt2.

candidates.title: Machine creation accepts flash drives (and NVRAMs) placed where the manual says they must not be (below RAM, not 2 MiB aligned, beyond 0x80000000+64TiB)
candidates.component: Machine creation from a configuration (machine_address_ranges::push_back_flash_drives / push_back_nvrams, machine_config::adjust_defaults)
candidates.role: Honest operator (creating the template is on the path 'Obtaining its valid template'); Low impact
candidates.location: src/machine-address-ranges.cpp push_back_flash_drives/push_back_nvrams (only overlap, 56-bit and page checks); src/hash-tree.cpp check_address_ranges (power-of-two alignment only); src/machine-config.cpp adjust_starts (auto-placement packs drives at their power-of-two length, so a drive shorter than 2 MiB after another gets a start that is not 2 MiB aligned); doc/README.md '### The board' (~7464-7470): 'Flash drives must start after 0x80000000+ram.length-1, end before 0x80000000+64TiB, and be aligned to 2MiB'; NVRAM length 'less than 128TiB'.
candidates.description: The manual states hard constraints on flash-drive placement (and an NVRAM length limit). The emulator enforces none of them: a 4 KiB flash drive at 0x10000000 (below RAM), one at 0x80101000 (not 2 MiB aligned) and a 2 MiB drive at 2^47 (past RAM+64TiB) are all accepted, and automatic placement itself can produce unaligned starts. The manual explains the constraints as Linux requirements, so the effect is a template whose drive Linux cannot map, not a wrong transition.
candidates.trigger: The trusted creator of a template (configuration), or default auto-placement of several small drives.
candidates.reachability: Configuration-level; any such template is a valid template as far as the emulator is concerned.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: possibly, as a trusted caller's configuration choice; reported for triage.
2 Role: machine creation, Honest operator per AUDIT.md.

3 High/Medium: none fits; R4 ('A configuration that would not [yield a machine on which this rule holds] is rejected') is not violated because the transition function, logs and proofs work on such machines.
4 Critical: no rule violated at a reachable state.
5 Low: a real discrepancy between the manual's 'must' and what the emulator accepts; 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller' -> Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None; an application author following the defaults may build a template whose drive the kernel refuses, a self-inflicted stall.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSPEC/flash.lua: start=0x10000000 len=0x1000 ACCEPTED; start=0x80101000 len=0x1000 ACCEPTED; start=0x800000000000 len=0x200000 ACCEPTED.
candidates.test_idea: Create machines with the three placements above and assert creation throws, unless the manual drops the 'must'.

not_covered: F and D floating-point semantics (soft-float rounding, NaN handling, fflags) against the RISC-V spec; the manual only names the extensions.
Exhaustive decode-space comparison (Zcb and reserved compressed encodings are pending as R1-R7-2; MNRET encoding checked only to fall through to an illegal-instruction exception).
Exception priority ordering and medeleg delegation corner cases beyond reading raise_exception.

PLIC register semantics (two contexts advertised in the DTB, one claim/complete address in code, hardwired priorities/enables): unreachable in reproducible machines because no PLIC source exists, so not pursued.
Hardware A/D-bit updates (no Svade, no menvcfg.ADUE) and D-bit setting on a failed SC: judged the default scheme of the current privileged spec, not reported.

AMO/LR/SC on device ranges (HTIF/CLINT/PLIC are R/W PMAs with no atomicity attribute in the manual): read and judged implementation-defined; only side-effecting PLIC claim reads could matter and they are unreachable in reproducible machines.
HTIF details beyond the code paths read (unknown devices/commands silently ignored, ihalt ignored, iyield bits other than 0/1); config-level validation of htif masks in reproducible templates.
The uarch's own architecture as documented (RV64I, 52 instructions, uarch shadow/RAM semantics) versus uarch-step.cpp and the Solidity step.
Manual statements in the host/Lua/JSON-RPC chapters (API semantics, CLI options other than the hash printers, store/load/clone documentation).
Other CLI claim builders (--mcycle-computation-hash, --uarch-cycle-computation-hash) were only read, not run across rejections; --initial-proof/--final-proof at a rejected yield not checked.
The manual's guest chapter (libcmt, rollup CLI, /dev/cmio) and the blockchain chapter's referee model versus Dave and doc/recipes.
Default DTB contents versus the manual's dtc listing beyond mmu-type, isa string, clint/plic/htif nodes (e.g. bootargs defaults, reserved-memory size).
